tagline.text: Garden paths, a pond-side chapel and shopping in central Makati

location.label: Location
location.text: Greenbelt complex, Ayala Center, San Lorenzo, Makati, Metro Manila

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Consider December–May for outdoor walks; combine indoor shopping and meals year-round

duration.label: Time needed
duration.text: Half a day, or a full day with a museum visit and meals

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱600–1,600 per person (illustrative half-day food and local transport budget; shopping and lodging excluded)

children.text: Greenbelt combines landscaped gardens, ponds, a chapel and retail wings in Makati’s Ayala Center. Alternate indoor browsing with short outdoor walks for a half-day visit, distinguishing the Greenbelt 1 redevelopment from Greenbelt 2’s ground-floor reopening in 2026.

The gardens between the buildings are central to the experience. Follow shade and water past retail, dining and worship spaces, even if shopping is not your main aim. Alternate outdoor walking with indoor breaks when heat or showers build; an umbrella and shoes with grip help on uncovered links.

The numbers identify wings, not a guarantee that all five are fully operating. Ayala Land describes Greenbelt 1 as a demolition-and-rebuild project, while July 2026 reporting gives a target reopening in 2028. Treat that as a target rather than a confirmed opening date.
Greenbelt, Glorietta and Landmark are distinct names within Ayala Center. Specify a Greenbelt wing when sharing your destination or arranging a taxi.

Greenbelt 2 reopened its ground floor in July 2026 with retail replacing former al fresco restaurants. This explains why older restaurant addresses may no longer work. Check the wing and level of your intended stops, then build around one garden circuit and one meal.
Use the chapel and pond as landmarks while exploring the gardens. Leave space for other walkers on bridges and stay outside planted areas.
See the low-domed chapel among trees and water, remembering that worship takes place here. Check the chapel’s dated notices if attending Mass and avoid intrusive photography.

Explore the reopened ground floor and use the current directory instead of older dining lists. The 2026 gallery image documents a post-reopening storefront, not completion of the entire redevelopment.
Browse international fashion with a focused list. Follow store photography rules and compare final prices, exchange rates and your destination’s import allowance before buying.
Pause for a meal or tea, choosing indoor or outdoor seating to suit your group. Check the current menu and whether tax and service charges are included.

blocks.title: Add Ayala Museum as a separate stop

children.text: The neighboring Ayala Museum adds history and art to the day. It has its own admission and operating arrangements; reduce shopping time if adding a proper exhibition visit.
Identify your arrival wing, level and return pickup point, then choose a meal and a few shops from the current directory.
Walk the garden, pond and chapel exterior in short shaded stretches; leave active worship undisturbed.
Choose the reopened Greenbelt 2 ground floor and selected areas of wings 3–5 instead of trying to cover everything.
Have an early dinner and return, allowing extra pickup time during rain or the evening rush.
Visit Ayala Museum first if open that day; otherwise substitute another Makati activity.
Lunch in Greenbelt, take a garden walk and locate toilets and lifts before the afternoon.
Browse selected shops, then depart from Ayala Center; allow a separate transfer if continuing to BGC.

MRT-3 Ayala provides rail access to Ayala Center. Follow current signs and pedestrian routes onward to Greenbelt, allowing time for wayfinding, crossings and security checks; indoor links may depend on mall operations.
Set a specific Greenbelt wing and pickup point. For MNL transfers, verify your terminal and use live traffic and booking estimates rather than a fixed fare or short journey promise.

Check safe crossings from your accommodation. Ask staff for lifts and accessible entrances when using a stroller or wheelchair. Drivers should check current parking rates and note the wing, level and bay.

Plan garden time around drier weather, while indoor browsing and dining remain year-round options. The periods below are general planning guidance, not a forecast; shorten outdoor walking during heavy rain or wind advisories.

blocks.label: Season at a glance
rows: Allow for weekend and holiday dining and traffic
Prepare for daytime heat and sun
Combine indoor breaks with short shaded walks
Rain, wind and transfer delays possible
Prioritize indoor stops and adjust garden time

children.text: For a quieter visit, consider a weekday outside meal peaks, while allowing for events, sales and religious services. Chapel, cinema and shop schedules differ, so check the relevant facility rather than applying one timetable to the whole complex.

The ₱600–1,600 range is an illustrative 2026 half-day allocation per person, not an official ticket, restaurant or transport tariff. Shopping, hotels, museum admission and cinema tickets are additional.

items.label: Meal allocation
items.note: Personal allocation, not a quoted menu price

items.label: Local transport allocation
items.note: May be exceeded; not an airport-transfer quote

children.text: Check tax, service charges and return conditions before paying. Price cinema tickets, paid exhibitions and parking separately using current booking or on-site information.

Fit Greenbelt into a Makati stay rather than changing accommodation solely for this visit. Compare actual walking entrances and crossings, not straight-line distance, and arrange luggage storage before a post-checkout visit.

Choose dining around seating and current waits as well as cuisine. Restaurant moves accompanied the Greenbelt 2 changes, so verify the present wing before booking and explain dietary needs before ordering.
Remember wing, level and entrance, and set a precise meeting point for your group.
Leave walking and security-check time between museum, meal and cinema bookings.
Gallery photographs span different years; older signs and renovation screens are historical records rather than a current directory.
Use designated pedestrian routes in rain and confirm the wing, entrance and vehicle plate before boarding a booked ride.
Respect construction barriers and follow temporary signs rather than assuming former links remain open.
Dress and behave respectfully at the chapel without obstructing worshippers or liturgical space.
Watch children near water, steps and bridges, especially after rain, and avoid grabbing or gathering animals with food.
Keep phones and wallets secure around busy entrances and tables, and arrange your return transport in advance.
Explore the wider city through Ayala Triangle Gardens, weekend markets and Poblacion; this entry adds detailed guidance for Greenbelt itself.
Continue to Taguig’s separate commercial district with time for a transfer and evening traffic.
